title: Data mid scenario data quality monitoring
topic: Data mid scenario data quality monitoring
question: How would you design monitoring so your team catches this kind of problem automatically instead of hearing about it from a confused executive?
idealAnswer:
Add automated data quality checks, e.g. null rate thresholds, row count checks, value range checks, that run as part of the pipeline rather than relying on humans eyeballing dashboards

Alert on anomalies, e.g. a sudden spike in null rates or a big swing in a key metric compared to historical patterns, rather than only checking whether the pipeline job succeeded or failed

Distinguish pipeline success, the job ran without error, from data correctness, the output values are actually right, since this incident is a case where the job 'succeeded' but produced wrong data

Consider failing the pipeline or quarantining the batch when a critical check fails, e.g. null rate above some threshold, rather than loading bad data through to the dashboard

A strong answer suggests tracking these quality metrics over time so the team can see trends, not just single-run pass/fail, and mentions involving the source system owners since the root cause was upstream

raw.context: Your company's revenue dashboard showed a sudden 40% drop yesterday. It turned out a source system started sending null values in a currency field, and your pipeline silently treated nulls as zero, so a chunk of real revenue was recorded as $0. Nobody noticed until a VP asked why the numbers looked wrong.
